## Strategy guide

**Draft strategy summary · Luna · SCPT episode 347, “Super L1Z1X Mindnet Guide” (published 2024-04-17)**  
Source transcript: complete ASR transcript, verified provenance in the extraction header; references below use its segment IDs and exact speech times. Ruleset compatibility has not been reviewed. The speakers give six-player advice and discuss Milty-style drafts only where identified. These are podcast recommendations, not rules rulings or measured win-rate results.

### Strategic thesis

L1Z1X is a high-variance faction whose tools are unusually concentrated in invasion, bombardment, fleet pressure, and taking structures. Those strengths do not automatically score points. The hosts describe games where L1 excels when the map, objectives, and table make violence productive, but sees weaker results when those advantages do not fit the revealed scoring environment. Their advice is to build the economic and technological base to threaten force, preserve enough tokens and mobility to act at the right moment, and keep a scoring path in view. **C01** (17:43–18:46; s000256, s000272).

The first selection is the slice. A high-influence slice helps pay for the many activations that a late-game strike may require; a blue skip eases the demanding blue technology route. The speakers say they would hesitate to draft L1 without substantial influence or a blue skip, ideally both. This is a warning about running out of gas, not a hard cutoff. **C02** (1:45:44–1:46:10; s001671, s001676).

### Round-one openings

**Diplomacy** is the safest leading option in the guide’s view. L1’s single five-resource home planet gives the card useful refresh value, and taking the card controls when that refresh occurs. The resources can support research and then production; more plastic on the board makes L1’s later threat credible. If a skip is available, Diplomacy also helps pay for the technology plan. The hosts say they consider it in almost every round, though that is an opinion rather than a universal pick order. **C03** (1:04:17–1:05:09; s000958, s000974).

**Leadership** is a middling alternative when the slice lacks influence or the table is likely to leave Diplomacy available as a follow. Its extra tokens can relieve L1’s weak home influence. But pick order matters: if Diplomacy is taken before L1 and Construction is the remaining card, Leadership may deliver tokens without enough early ships to use them. Judge the card by the actual slice and expected follow, rather than the raw token count. **C04** (1:01:01–1:02:09; s000900, s000920).

**Trade** may be best when the table supports debt-meta and commodity washing. Trade goods solve a central L1 weakness because they can be spent flexibly. Yet L1 starts without a trade ship, so neighbors may need to come to you. The discussion compares a potentially strong Diplomacy refresh against Trade’s replenishment and neighbor payments; it concludes that table cooperation and access change the comparison. Favor Trade when you can reliably convert it into trade goods, while recognizing that Diplomacy can produce more immediate raw resources in some round-one positions. **C05** (1:09:45–1:10:57; s001050, s001073).

The guide discourages defaulting to **Warfare** simply to expand farther. L1 already begins with capacity for its opening two-carrier-equivalent force, and the hosts prefer a concentrated home build that creates a stronger round-two fleet and round-three threat. Warfare can still be right when a particular map or objective makes reach more valuable than fleet quality. **C06** (1:12:30–1:13:34; s001100, s001122).

**Technology** is the higher-ceiling opening when funds and a follow make double research feasible. It addresses L1’s awkward starting colors and makes its kit work better, but requires an unusually large investment. The hosts contrast that upside with a reliable but lower-ceiling opening; they do not claim every L1 should take Technology or that taking its secondary is free. **C07** (1:13:42–1:15:05; s001123, s001143).

### Technology and economy

The no-skip route centers on **Gravity Drive**, **Super Dreadnought II**, and **Carrier II**. Gravity Drive improves flagship reach; the dreadnought upgrade supports the faction’s defining ships; Carrier II makes better use of the home dock’s production. The hosts acknowledge that this line consumes many rounds of research and should be adapted to actual tempo. A yellow skip can instead support an early Cruiser II detour before returning to the dreadnought route. This is a situational option when the cruiser has a job and research is affordable, not a default extra upgrade. **C08** (1:18:20–1:19:06; s001209, s001215). **C10** (1:21:32–1:22:24; s001256, s001272).

With a blue skip, the hosts prefer using it to get Gravity Drive early, then considering AI Development Algorithm as a way to reach Super Dreadnought II or Carrier II. They encourage using the skip repeatedly when the game’s research tempo supports it. These are strategic route suggestions; this summary does not verify the current prerequisite rules for each line. **C09** (1:24:21–1:25:15; s001304, s001316).

The speakers strongly discourage routine **Inheritance Systems** research. They consider the two-yellow prerequisite route and the need to exhaust it and spend two resources at research too expensive relative to the effect. That is a forceful podcast judgment, not a rules or value ruling; unusual technology tempo or a particular objective could change an individual player’s calculation. **C11** (39:16–40:26; s000590, s000615).

The economic constraint is larger than a shortage of spendable resources. L1 has a five-resource home system and strong production, but only two commodities and a promissory note whose sale value the hosts openly dispute. One speaker treats it as roughly one trade good, another would pay more in a desperate situation. The guide advises treating the note as a useful one-time sale rather than a repeat income stream, while not expecting it to repair the economy by itself. It also notes that L1’s faction technologies have little synergy with its starting green and red technologies, making research feel even more costly. **C05** (Trade comparison above; s001050–s001073). **C07** (technology timing above). The note’s exact price remains contested in the episode; no fixed price is asserted here.

### Turning combat into advantage

L1’s starting Super Dreadnought and carrier can move an opening two-carrier, four-infantry force, giving the faction a workable initial expansion. The five-resource home planet supports a powerful production step, though its lack of influence remains a real limitation. The guide favors getting useful plastic onto the board rather than assuming the opening fleet alone will win anything. **C14** (30:24–30:48; s000458, s000463).

**Assimilate** makes an invasion more valuable when the target planet contains an enemy PDS or space dock: the host says the structure becomes an L1 unit before the tactical action’s production step, potentially letting the invader build there immediately. This is a concrete reason to value a structured planet, but it requires winning control and having resources, production capacity, and timing to use the opportunity. **C12** (28:24–28:50; s000429, s000434).

**Harrow** applies ships’ bombardment after each ground-combat round. The hosts describe it as a powerful way to swing close invasions, especially with Super Dreadnoughts in the active system. Treat it as extra pressure that can decide a close fight, not a guarantee: the system must contain ships with bombardment and the invasion must still be worth making. **C13** (29:08–30:29; s000444, s000458).

The faction flagship **0.0.1** puts pressure on opposing fleets by requiring its and L1 dreadnought hits in the system to be assigned to non-fighter ships when possible. The hosts recommend integrating the flagship into the larger plan because it can remove high-value ships and reduce the efficiency of fleets that rely on fighters to protect their hitters. They also note that fighters still absorb hits and that some compositions, such as Letnev’s, resist this particular pressure. Use the flagship for the matchup it improves, rather than treating its presence as a guaranteed fleet win. **C15** (31:06–31:44; s000470, s000477).

The mech’s bombardment text prompts an explicit caution in the discussion: once committed to a planet, the mech cannot continue bombarding. The hosts generally value its ground-combat presence and sustain more than leaving it in space to preserve another bombardment source. Decide based on the actual invasion; the episode itself explores edge cases and this summary does not settle them as rules. **C16** (32:26–33:23; s000488, s000503).

The hero, **The Helmsman**, offers a dramatic reposition of the flagship and any number of dreadnoughts into a system without other players’ ships. The speakers value this as a way to create a threat or set up an attack, while warning that opponents can occupy strategically important empty systems and limit destinations. The hero, flagship, and dreadnought package can therefore reward advance planning and visible threat projection. **C17** (47:43–48:57; s000716, s000735).

### Diplomacy, timing, and scoring

The hosts distinguish credible leverage from extortion. A visible fleet can make L1’s offers more persuasive, but threats for payment that does not advance a real goal may damage relationships. They prefer equitable arrangements tied to points or useful exchanges. A large invasion can be justified for a point, an objective, or a meaningful board position; a strike that only eliminates a rival may leave L1 defending an exposed fleet and unable to score afterward. Preserve enough mobility and political goodwill to convert force into a later win. **C18** (1:31:02–1:33:22; s001406, s001441). **C19** (1:33:30–1:34:31; s001442, s001458).

The guide’s preferred posture is to stay in the scoring pack while keeping force available for a decisive late-game “winslay.” It describes an ideal L1 position as third or fourth before the final strike, with enough command tokens and movement to affect the relevant systems. Stopping a leader can be useful, but only if L1 also has a path to score; preventing another player from winning is not itself a victory plan. **C20** (1:35:02–1:35:58; s001464, s001481).

L1 is not naturally strong at bonus points, agendas, economy objectives, or custodians in the hosts’ assessment. Its combat strength also does not equal control: planets must be held and enough tokens retained for activations. The guide suggests a possible late pivot into structure objectives by taking opposing structures with Assimilate, rather than spending early tokens and resources on Construction. That pivot is conditional: opponents’ structures must be reachable and capturable, and point-blocking can create political costs. **C21** (1:37:50–1:38:40; s001514, s001530). **C22** (1:38:41–1:39:01; s001531, s001542).

Mecatol Rex and Imperial can form a catch-up line, but the guide warns against assuming that merely taking Mecatol scores a public objective or enables another score in status. The plan depends on which objectives are revealed, qualification, secrets, and sufficient tempo. If scoring requirements do not line up, taking Mecatol may still help, but it can also consume scarce tokens and attention. Treat each objective’s actual prerequisites separately from partial preparation. **C23** (1:39:22–1:41:32; s001549, s001582).

The episode connects starting Plasma Scoring and bombardment to combat-oriented secrets such as **Turn Their Fleets to Dust** and **Make an Example of Their World**. This is an opportunity, not automatic scoring: the board and the specific objective’s timing conditions still matter. The speakers explicitly discuss a wording change and say Harrow’s later bombardment is not the same as the bombardment step for Make an Example; do not use the general combat synergy to erase that distinction. **C24** (1:41:33–1:42:12; s001583, s001598).

If the public objectives push the game toward stage-two tempo, the hosts see potential in L1’s reach for suitable late control or structure objectives, including distant territories and some single-target objectives. Tokens and actual objective requirements remain the constraint; even combat-oriented L1 may lack enough influence to activate all the systems its plan requires. **C25** (1:42:52–1:44:10; s001616, s001642).

### Counters and draft context

Opponents can blunt L1 by denying clean empty systems for the hero, defending valuable structures, avoiding unnecessary fleet exposure, and forcing L1 to spend activations without scoring. The guide’s own counterplay implications are conditional rather than a blanket prescription: occupying a hero destination matters only if that system would otherwise support L1’s plan, and denying a structure matters most when Assimilate or an objective makes it valuable. L1’s best response is to keep enough economic and token flexibility to change targets rather than commit everything to one visible invasion. **C12, C17, C20, C22**.

For Milty-style drafts specifically, the hosts propose taking L1 around third or fourth to seek a high-influence slice, then accepting a later speaker position from which Diplomacy may still be available. Their logic is that L1 is not usually an early faction pick and can remain viable with later speaker order. This advice assumes that draft order, slice options, and card availability cooperate; it is not presented as a universal map-making recommendation. **C26** (1:47:34–1:48:21; s001696, s001708).

### Uncertainty and scope

This summary reflects one 2024 podcast episode. The extraction header identifies a complete transcript produced with faster-whisper small.en on CPU; the text is ASR, so proper names and some terms may be misheard. “Winslay” and the hosts’ note valuation are preserved as their strategic language and contested opinion. The guide itself discusses an Omega wording change for Make an Example and prior component changes, but this work does not establish which current ruleset is in force. No claims here have been checked against a current rulebook, tournament setup, engine legality, or actual win-rate dataset. Citations point to transcript timestamps and segment IDs; the accompanying JSON carries component references and claim-level traceability.

<details><summary>upstream-community — The L1Z1X Mindnet (`l1z1x`)</summary>

[Exact pinned section](../sources/upstream-community.md#the-l1z1x-mindnet-l1z1x) · [Repository source](https://github.com/Feelx234/TI4-Bot-Dev/blob/1fd3092ad83a72bc3e379ac3946852b409adee6d/crates/ti4-server/docs/COMMUNITY_FACTION_STRATEGIES.md#the-l1z1x-mindnet-l1z1x)

> Historical source excerpt; advice and engine claims retain the source’s assumptions.

**Engine check.** Home [0.0.0] 5/0 (one planet); start 1 dreadnought, 1 carrier, 3 fighters, 5
infantry, dock, PDS; starting techs Neural Motivator and Plasma Scoring; 2 commodities. Super
Dreadnought I (capacity 2, bombardment 5); Super Dreadnought II (BBY: combat 4, move 2,
bombardment 4, immune to Direct Hit). Assimilate: take over PDS and docks on captured planets.
Harrow: bombard again after each ground-combat round. Inheritance Systems (YY). Commander (4
dreadnoughts on the board): bombard through planetary shields. Hero: move the flagship and all
dreadnoughts into one system.

**Opening and cards.** Expand to two systems next to home, research, build; Technology and
Leadership are the go-to cards, Technology using the 5-resource home; Warfare is "cracked"; with
the rich home even Diplomacy is a fine last pick ([r/ti "How to play L1Z1X?", 2022](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/ssbfzw/how_to_play_l1z1x/)).

**Technology.** Super Dreadnought II is the bread and butter, through blue (Antimass or a skip,
Gravity Drive) rather than the yellow faction line: the blue route gets there as fast and its
techs are useful; Inheritance Systems is "near useless in a 10-point game". Sarween early helps
unlock the commander (four dreadnoughts). Skips steer the rest: green skip for Hyper Metabolism or
Infantry II; Destroyer II or Fighter II against fighter swarms; PDS II is board dependent.
Disagreement: a minority likes Inheritance Systems into War Suns against PDS-heavy opponents (same
thread).

**Builds and targets.** Dreadnoughts with infantry inside (capacity 2); add 2-3 infantry at home with
each build to make the one-planet home untakeable. Target forward docks and PDS: Assimilate takes
them and a captured dock can produce the same turn. L1Z1X are natural Mecatol Rex holders and the
faction most able to knock Sol off it. Pressure Arborec early ([r/ti 2022](https://www.reddit.com/r/twilightimperium/comments/w6o8y9/how_to_destroy_arborec_as_l1z1x/)).

**Threats.** Fighter swarms (cheap hit absorption), Yin (Impulse Core, Devotion, Indoctrination of
the few infantry), Sardakk; Direct Hit before Super Dreadnought II. Play the "scary dreadnought
faction, do not mess with me" card diplomatically rather than attacking everyone.

**Strength.** SCPT row 2 (2022), C (2025); async PoK C.

**Bot feasibility.**
- Research: Gravity Drive (via Antimass or a skip), Super Dreadnought II, then Destroyer II or
  Fighter II when neighbours field fighters. Value medium, effort S.
- Build mix: dreadnoughts with two infantry each, plus 2-3 infantry kept at home. Effort S.
- Targeting: in `activation_value`, an enemy PDS or dock on a takeable planet is worth its cost to
  L1Z1X (Assimilate); today structures only count against the attacker. Value medium, effort S-M.
- Fight model: add Harrow to the ground-combat estimate (`ground_needed`), so the bot lands fewer
  infantry when its dreadnoughts are present. Value medium, effort M.

</details>

- **Kit**: `ps`, `nm` start; dreadnought, carrier, 3 fighters, 5 infantry, PDS. Assimilate
  (take structures), Harrow (bombard during ground combat). Own dreadnought (capacity 2),
  `sdn2` Super Dreadnought II (BBY: combat 4, move 2, capacity 2), `is` Inheritance Systems
  (YY). Flagship makes dreadnought hits hit non-fighters. Commander at 4 dreadnoughts.
- **Mid**: build dreadnoughts to four (commander), take the strongest neighbouring systems.
  **Late**: super-dreadnought stack with fighter screen through to the objectives.

  blue (two) and one yellow.
- **Build**: mid dreadnoughts (to 3-4), one carrier, fighters; late dreadnoughts (5), flagship.
- **Cards/tokens**: Warfare; fleet pool large enough for the dreadnought stack.
- **Pitfalls**: bombarding without the infantry to land; slow fleet without `gd`/`sdn2`.

<details><summary>Structured claims, conditions and source citations</summary>

## Strategy claims

<a id="claim-c01"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat L1 as a high-variance combat faction whose strength depends on whether objectives, map, and table make its unusually strong invasion and fleet tools relevant.
  Conditions: Best fit when combat can convert into points or useful leverage; performance may be poor when the game emphasizes economy. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Hosts’ assessment, not tournament data.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 1064–1126s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md)
<a id="claim-c02"></a>

- **Draft:** Prioritize a high-influence slice, ideally with a blue skip, because tokens sustain repeated activations and a blue skip eases the costly technology path.
  Conditions: Especially important in six-player and tournament contexts; reconsider L1 if both are absent. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Map-dependent advice; no exact influence threshold is asserted.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 6338–6367s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md)
<a id="claim-c03"></a>

- **Draft:** Use Diplomacy as a leading round-one option to refresh the five-resource home planet, control timing, and fund technology or production.
  Conditions: Attractive when the planet is ready to refresh and timing lets you exploit resources twice; consider skips and slice resources. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Hosts rank it highly but call Trade better in some tables.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 3857–3909s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Diplomacy](../components.md#strategy-card-pok2diplomacy)
<a id="claim-c04"></a>

- **Draft:** Consider Leadership when the slice is influence-poor and Diplomacy is likely to remain available for a follow; its tokens help a faction with no home influence.
  Conditions: Less attractive if Diplomacy is taken before you or Construction rather than Diplomacy is the final pick. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Hosts call Leadership middling and table-order dependent.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 3662–3730s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Leadership](../components.md#strategy-card-pok1leadership)
<a id="claim-c05"></a>

- **Draft:** Prefer Trade when the table cooperates with debt-meta and commodity washing, since trade goods address L1’s structural economic weakness.
  Conditions: More valuable with reachable, willing neighbors; without a trade ship, neighbors must come to you, so early cash may trail Diplomacy. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Hosts compare conditional cases and disagree on exact note value.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 4178–4257s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Trade](../components.md#strategy-card-pok5trade)
<a id="claim-c06"></a>

- **Draft:** Do not default to Warfare just to spread farther: the opening already has two-capacity ships, and a concentrated rollout can make L1 a stronger round-three threat.
  Conditions: Use Warfare when map or objective makes reach more valuable than a stronger fleet build. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Preferred plan, not prohibition.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 4347–4415s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Warfare](../components.md#strategy-card-pok6warfare)
<a id="claim-c07"></a>

- **Draft:** Technology is the ambitious round-one pick when a double research compensates for awkward starting colors; it has a higher ceiling but depends on economy and follows.
  Conditions: Choose when funds and Diplomacy or Trade make the secondary affordable. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Hosts call Tech a ceiling play yet describe the opening as expensive.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 4416–4505s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Technology](../components.md#strategy-card-pok7technology)
<a id="claim-c08"></a>

- **Draft:** With no skip, aim toward Gravity Drive, Super Dreadnought II, and Carrier II for flagship movement, dreadnought reach, and capacity for home production.
  Conditions: A demanding multi-round plan; adapt to tempo and funds. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Recommended path, not required sequence or rules audit.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 4700–4741s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Gravity Drive](../components.md#technology-gd), [Super Dreadnought II](../components.md#technology-sdn2), [Carrier II](../components.md#technology-cv2)
<a id="claim-c09"></a>

- **Draft:** A blue skip can accelerate Gravity Drive in round one and then be spent on Super Dreadnought II or Carrier II through AI Development Algorithm.
  Conditions: Exploit the skip repeatedly when research tempo permits. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Exact prerequisite legality was not independently checked.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5060–5115s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Gravity Drive](../components.md#technology-gd), [AI Development Algorithm](../components.md#technology-aida), [Super Dreadnought II](../components.md#technology-sdn2), [Carrier II](../components.md#technology-cv2)
<a id="claim-c10"></a>

- **Draft:** A yellow skip offers a situational early Cruiser II detour, then can help resume the core dreadnought path.
  Conditions: Consider when research is affordable and the cruiser has a concrete job. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Modest alternative, not default.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 4892–4945s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Cruiser II](../components.md#technology-cr2), [Super Dreadnought II](../components.md#technology-sdn2)
<a id="claim-c11"></a>

- **Draft:** Do not chase Inheritance Systems routinely; the hosts regard its two-yellow path and two-resource activation as too costly.
  Conditions: Reconsider only with unusual technology tempo or a specific objective. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Strong podcast opinion; current value unverified.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 2350–2426s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Inheritance Systems](../components.md#technology-is)
<a id="claim-c12"></a>

- **Draft:** Assimilate makes a planet with an enemy PDS or space dock unusually valuable because the structure becomes an L1 copy before tactical-action production.
  Conditions: Requires taking such a planet and an opportunity to produce afterward. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Timing is the hosts’ account; full rules legality not reviewed.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 1699–1731s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Assimilate](../components.md#ability-assimilate), [PDS I](../components.md#unit-pds), [Space Dock I](../components.md#unit-spacedock)
<a id="claim-c13"></a>

- **Draft:** Harrow can turn a close ground invasion into a win by applying ships’ bombardment after each ground-combat round.
  Conditions: Most relevant when bombardment ships are in the active system and the invasion is contested. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Conditional advantage, not automatic win.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 1748–1824s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Harrow](../components.md#ability-harrow), [Super Dreadnought I](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-dreadnought)
<a id="claim-c14"></a>

- **Draft:** Use the starting Super Dreadnought’s two capacity with the carrier to move the opening 2C4I force.
  Conditions: Account for distance and ground-force needs. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Opening fleet called adequate; expansion depends on slice.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 1822–1848s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Super Dreadnought I](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-dreadnought), [Carrier I](../components.md#unit-carrier), [Infantry I](../components.md#unit-infantry)
<a id="claim-c15"></a>

- **Draft:** The L1 flagship rewards joining it with dreadnoughts: its hits force assignment to non-fighter ships when possible, pressuring fighter-based fleets.
  Conditions: Useful for a major battle or to deter attacks in its system. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Fighters still provide hit points and some matchups resist this pressure.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 1865–1904s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [\[0.0.1\]](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-flagship), [Super Dreadnought I](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-dreadnought)
<a id="claim-c16"></a>

- **Draft:** Do not leave mechs in space just to preserve bombardment; once committed to a planet they cannot bombard, and ground-combat sustain is usually more valuable.
  Conditions: Choose based on whether bombardment or ground presence changes the invasion. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Transcript discusses edge cases; strategic point is clearer than rules details.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 1947–2003s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Anihilator](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-mech), [Harrow](../components.md#ability-harrow)
<a id="claim-c17"></a>

- **Draft:** The Helmsman can reposition the flagship and dreadnoughts into an empty system, creating a late threat and surprise attack option.
  Conditions: Destination must lack other players’ ships; opponents can occupy key systems to limit options. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Reflects guide text and 2024 discussion; current rules unchecked.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 2862–2938s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The Helmsman](../components.md#leader-l1z1xhero), [\[0.0.1\]](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-flagship), [Super Dreadnought I](../components.md#unit-l1z1x-dreadnought)
<a id="claim-c18"></a>

- **Draft:** Project credible force to improve bargaining, but avoid extortion that earns little while damaging future relations.
  Conditions: Seek equitable point-enabling trades; explain the peaceful deal and preserve mobility for scoring. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Table-dependent political advice.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5460–5602s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md)
<a id="claim-c19"></a>

- **Draft:** Avoid a major invasion that only removes a rival if it leaves L1 with an exposed fleet, weak mobility, and no path to score.
  Conditions: War can be worthwhile for a point, objective, or meaningful leverage. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Common failure pattern, not absolute rule.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5603–5676s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md)
<a id="claim-c20"></a>

- **Draft:** Use combat to threaten or execute a decisive late-game winslay while remaining in the scoring pack; the ideal is a strong third- or fourth-place position before that window.
  Conditions: Needs command tokens, mobility, technology, and fleet to reach relevant systems; do not spend the game stopping others without a scoring plan. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Hosts’ strategic framing; no victory guarantee.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5698–5758s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md), [The Helmsman](../components.md#leader-l1z1xhero)
<a id="claim-c21"></a>

- **Draft:** Prepare to pivot into structure objectives by taking opposing structures with Assimilate instead of routinely buying them through Construction.
  Conditions: May appeal late, even after an opponent scores, when taking a structure advances or blocks an objective. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Control is not guaranteed and aggressive point blocking has political cost.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5868–5919s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Assimilate](../components.md#ability-assimilate), [Build Defenses](../components.md#public-objective-build-defenses), [Construct Massive Cities](../components.md#public-objective-massive-cities)
<a id="claim-c22"></a>

- **Draft:** Combat strength does not itself satisfy control objectives: plan to hold planets, retain command tokens, and meet each objective’s prerequisites.
  Conditions: Especially important for stage-two or multi-system control objectives. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: High-level advice; every objective requirement is not enumerated.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5920–5941s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md)
<a id="claim-c23"></a>

- **Draft:** Treat Mecatol Rex plus Imperial as a possible catch-up line, but do not assume taking Mecatol scores a stage one or enables a second status-phase score.
  Conditions: Requires revealed objectives, qualification, and sufficient tempo; prerequisites and secrets can make it poor. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Not a scoring-rules verification.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 5957–6093s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Imperial](../components.md#strategy-card-pok8imperial), [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md)
<a id="claim-c24"></a>

- **Draft:** Starting Plasma Scoring and bombardment can help with combat secrets such as Turn Their Fleets to Dust or Make an Example of Their World.
  Conditions: Select only when board state and exact objective timing/conditions align. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Guide notes wording change; do not infer Harrow counts as the bombardment step.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 6094–6137s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [Plasma Scoring](../components.md#technology-ps), [Turn Their Fleets to Dust](../components.md#secret-objective-ttfd), [Make an Example of Their World](../components.md#secret-objective-mew), [Harrow](../components.md#ability-harrow)
<a id="claim-c25"></a>

- **Draft:** If the game trends toward stage-two tempo, use movement and combat to pursue suitable late control or structure objectives; some single-target objectives may fit L1’s reach.
  Conditions: Only when mobility, tokens, and actual requirements align; outside-home structure objectives are an exception. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Tendency, not guaranteed scoring.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 6169–6250s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The Helmsman](../components.md#leader-l1z1xhero), [Rule Distant Lands](../components.md#public-objective-distant-lands), [Construct Massive Cities](../components.md#public-objective-massive-cities)
<a id="claim-c26"></a>

- **Draft:** In Milty-style draft, the guide proposes taking L1 around third or fourth to pursue a high-influence slice, then accepting a later speaker pick that can take Diplomacy.
  Conditions: Depends on L1 not being an early faction pick and draft availability. Compatibility: SCPT347, published 2024-04-17; ruleset compatibility unreviewed. Uncertainty: Specific draft advice, not universal map-making advice.
  Sources: [SCPT 347 6449–6501s](https://spacecatspeaceturtles.podbean.com/e/347-super-l1z1x-mindnet-guide/)
  Components: [The L1Z1X Mindnet](l1z1x.md), [Diplomacy](../components.md#strategy-card-pok2diplomacy)
